e-7901.knowledge_point: Solving Inequalities Requiring Multiplication by a Positive Factor
e-7901.worked_solution:
We know that the denominator $5x^4+ 2$ is positive for all values of $x.$ So, we can multiply both sides of the inequality by $5x^4+2$ and solve the resulting inequality as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{5{x}^{4}+2} & <\frac{5-2x}{5{x}^{4}+2} \\ (5{x}^{4}+2)\cdot \frac{2}{5{x}^{4}+2} & <(5{x}^{4}+2)\cdot \frac{5-2x}{5{x}^{4}+2} \\ 2 & <5-2x \\ 2x & <3 \\ x & <\frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 2
after.worked_solution:
We know that the denominator ${x}^{4}+2$ is positive for all values of $x.$ So, we can multiply both sides of the inequality by ${x}^{4}+2$ and solve the resulting inequality as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2{x}^{4}+3x}{{x}^{4}+2} & \le 2 \\ ({x}^{4}+2)\cdot \frac{2{x}^{4}+3x}{{x}^{4}+2} & \le ({x}^{4}+2)\cdot 2 \\ 2{x}^{4}+3x & \le 2{x}^{4}+4 \\ 3x & \le 4 \\ x & \le \frac{4}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

content.worked_solution:
We know that the denominator ${x}^{4}+2$ is positive for all values of $x.$ So, we can multiply both sides of the inequality by ${x}^{4}+2$ and solve the resulting inequality as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2{x}^{4}+3x}{{x}^{4}+2} & \le 2 \\ ({x}^{4}+2)\cdot \frac{2{x}^{4}+3x}{{x}^{4}+2} & \le ({x}^{4}+2)\cdot 2 \\ 2{x}^{4}+3x & \le 2{x}^{4}+4 \\ 3x & \le 4 \\ x & \le \frac{4}{3}\end{aligned}
$$
